text:
Alex K: heads-up — provisioning stalled for several new gpu nodes in ap-northeast-1 since ~02:10 UTC. nodes spin up then fail kubelet/registration. :eyes:
Maria P: saw alerts. we deployed a default-deny egress fw policy last night for the region (ticket #INF-8271). suspect it's blocking the node-agent -> iam/token and audit-export endpoints.
Sanjay R: confirmed from node logs: "POST https://iam.internal/token 403 TLS handshake reset" and "connection refused logging-shipper.internal:443". pasted a snippet below.
Sanjay R: ```
Feb 21 02:14:22 kubelet[123]: E [auth] token fetch failed: POST https://iam.internal/token -> 403
Feb 21 02:14:25 node-agent[1]: WARN audit exporter: dial tcp 10.10.5.22:443: connection reset by peer
```
Jen L: quick triage options:
- Add minimal egress allowlist for iam.internal + logging-shipper + apt/os-update endpoints (temporary)
- Roll back default-deny for ap-northeast-1 until we get a scoped policy
- Or spin up a shared NAT gateway in the warm-pool subnets for node bootstrap (but costs per-AZ apply) :money_with_wings:
Ryan T: cost notes: a single NAT per-AZ is ~ $0.06/hr + data. For 3 AZs that's ~ $13/day baseline; central NAT shared across >1 cluster adds complexity but cheaper than widening fw by IP ranges long-term.
Maria P: policy design proposal: allow egress only to these FQDNs and tag-based destinations: iam.internal, logging-shipper.internal, deb-mirrors.redwood.com. TTL on the allowlist entries 48h, then review. keeps default-deny but unblocks bootstrap.
Alex K: can we do a canary: apply allowlist to one AZ / warm-pool only and try 5 nodes? if they join, expand.
Jen L: yes. plan:
1) update fw rule ap-northeast-1-warmpool-egress (allow iam.internal, logging-shipper.internal, deb-mirrors)
2) create 5-node warmpool canary (tag: fw-canary=apn1)
3) monitor kubelet registration & audit export for 15m
Config snippet for the fw rule:```hcl
resource "firewall_rule" "warmpool_allow" {
  name = "apn1-warmpool-egress-allow"
  vpc  = "vpc-xxxx"
  egress = [
    {to = "iam.internal", ports = [443]},
    {to = "logging-shipper.internal", ports = [443]},
    {to = "deb-mirrors.redwood.com", ports = [80,443]}
  ]
  ttl = 48h
}
```
Sanjay R: note: the audit exporter can buffer but we saw node-agent OOM when it retried a lot; keep buffer config conservative for canary. also add ephemeral rule for apt mirrors so nodes can apt-get during bootstrap.
Ryan T: ping on cost/regulatory: ap-northeast logging endpoint must stay internal (no public egress), so NAT approach will need strict egress-only proxies with TLS inspection off — regulatory OK but ops-heavy.
Alex K: ok assigning tasks: Maria update fw rule canary; Jen spin warmpool nodes; Sanjay watch logs & collector; Ryan assemble cost delta (nat vs scoped allowlist) in channel. timeframe: aim to have canary live in next 30m.
OpsBot: Created incident INF-8420: "ap-northeast gpu provisioning blocked by new egress default-deny" assigned to @Maria P. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8420 :lock:
Maria P: starting rule patch now, I'll post the diff once up. :thumbsup:
Alex K: thanks — please post results (success/failure) and last 3 lines of kubelet log if it fails.
Maria P: patch applied to ap-northeast-1-warmpool-egress (ttl=48h). canary warmpool request created.
Sanjay R: canary nodes started and joined at 02:38 UTC. audit export showed a few transient retries then healthy. marking canary green. :white_check_mark:
Alex K: great. plan for tomorrow: formalize FQDN allowlist and automate TTL rollback. also review audit retention cost impact of moving more traffic through NAT.
Ryan T: I'll model NAT vs allowlist cost + ops overhead, share by EOD.
Jen L: follow-up action: add an automated smoke test that runs kubelet registration + audit export after fw policy updates. low-effort but will save future incidents.
Alex K: agreed. closing thread after action items noted.
